outcome.technical: P155-R23 (restore_copy's two refusals saying 'the next move drops it'): fixed by the finding's resolution, not by rewording alone - a reworded refusal would describe a dead end, since unsettled_stop stops dispatch and integration over a standing copy before any move runs. _worktrees.restore_copy now settles both shapes the way _resume does: a copy with no index.json is dropped (new _dropped helper: restored None, the error saying the copy was dropped and the tree is settled; a drop that fails stays restored False with the copy kept); the copy of a move the marker recorded (base == end) goes to new _settle_recorded, which drops it when _newer_work over heads (end,) names nothing and otherwise keeps it naming every diverging path and saying no move, restore, dispatch or integration takes it down over newer work. The base-not-in-(start,end) refusal is unchanged. Cases un14 (no index.json dropped, tree_unsettled False after, no byte changed, HEAD at base), un15 (recorded move copy dropped, HEAD at head), un16 (over-fire twin: recorded move with newer work kept, a.txt and c.txt named, no byte changed, no 'next move' in the text). drive-phase restore_tree renders restored None as before ('nothing restored - <error>', E_USAGE), so the drop reads through it unchanged. P155-R60 (ut5's first-site and every-caller rules had no failing case): added ut6 (planted twice(): removal, tree_unsettled, second removal: named; its twin once() asking before both: not named) and ut7 (planted remover() with callers asks_first and asks_after: named; twin covered() whose two callers both ask first: not named). Proven by mutation of the scanner in a scratch exec of the test source (no file written): min to max turns ut6 red with ut5 and ut7 green; all to any turns ut7 red with ut5 and ut6 green - which also confirms the finding that ut5 alone could not tell them apart. These two cases pass on HEAD by construction because the scanner lives in the test file. P155-R68 (native_spelling only covered the unsettled family): manage-worktrees do_remove and do_task_remove now name the tree through _wt.native_spelling in every refusal naming a tree git listed - main-tree, standing-inside, not-described, dirty, and the other tasks' trees listed when none is this one's; argv and the removed field keep git's spelling. drive-phase add_tree records the tree verb's path through _worktrees.native_spelling, and every task tree the drive's state names later (wave trees, keptTrees, recuts) is that record or derived from it. Evidence for the drive half: task-add's answer was already os.path.abspath at both arms (do_task_add target, adopt_task_tree), and ntpath.abspath('C:/r/t') returns the backslash spelling (observed), so the stops the finding lists were already native in practice; add_tree now holds it whatever the verb returns. restore_copy's own messages naming the tree are spelled the same way. The finding's 'spell at the source (list_worktrees record)' was not taken: parse_list's documented contract is the path exactly as git printed it, read by modules outside this task's files (close-phase, integrate-task, panel, doctor, run-test-gate, stamp-verification), and the work order names the one helper at the refusal sites.
